newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Tension rises in Zaire diamond-mining centre.
newsitem.headline: Tension rises in Zaire diamond-mining centre.

text.p: Mbuji-Mayi, the centre of Zaire's Kasai diamond mining region, is in a state of high tension after troops stopped local protests against Lebanese businessmen, witnesses said on Sunday.

"Troops encircled the town on Saturday and prevented a planned demonstration, but tension is high and people are afraid something may happen later this week," one expatriate witness contacted by telephone said.
Military sources in Kinshasa said soldiers had been moved in to the area in recent weeks.
Diamonds which since the collapse of copper and cobalt mining have become Zaire's main foreign currency earner come in large part from the Kasai region.
Kasai is a hotbed of opposition to President Mobutu Sese Seko and home of radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi.

The region has since 1993 used different money from the rest of the chaotic Central African state, after the radical opposition refused to accept the new zaire currency introduced to replace the old money.
